cards.headline: Written drunk in Soho, meant as a cry for help
cards.snippet: In 1995, Underworld released "Born Slippy .NUXX" as a B-side. Its vocalist Karl Hyde had written the lyrics after a night of drinking on Wardour Street in Soho, London, while deep in alcoholism. He wanted to capture how a drunk sees the world in fragments, with only small pieces of memory left afterwards. Audiences later raised lager cans during performances, which disturbed him. Hyde said he meant the song as a cry for help, not a drinking anthem.
cards.context: Hyde was deep in alcoholism at the time.

cards.headline: "Lager, lager, lager" came from losing his place
cards.snippet: In a 2006 interview with The Guardian, Underworld vocalist Karl Hyde explained how "Born Slippy" came together. He recorded the vocals in one take. Whenever he lost his place, he sang the same line again, and that is where "lager, lager, lager, lager" came from. The title has a separate origin: Born Slippy was a greyhound the band had won money on.
